summary: Single scene sc_001 (0-78000 ms, interior woodland cottage, day into evening). On-screen evidence shows Juliana examining a worn herbal book and Alexander sharing knowledge of yarrow, soldier survival, and his scars, ending with Juliana's shift in view of wealth. Uncertainty: the on-screen events do not show Juliana's mother's death, the nature of the war, or Alexander's background beyond the dialogue, so these are reported only as spoken. The supplied metadata (logline and continuity notes) is not on-screen evidence and is unverified; it was not used for beats or revelations. characters.name: Juliana
characters.role: Woman examining her mother's worn herbal book; her mother wrote it over years according to her dialogue

characters.name: Alexander
characters.role: Scarred man who brings yarrow, shares plant knowledge, and references soldiering and war

beats.description: Juliana handles the aged leather herbal book, warns that some pages are ruined, and says her mother spent years writing it.
Alexander enters the dim room and sets a bundle of white herbal flowers beside the open book.
Juliana identifies yarrow; Alexander says it treats wounds and fever and that soldiers learn which plants keep a man alive.
Juliana offers to trim Alexander's hair and beard; he catches her wrist and says not yet and let them grow.
Juliana teases him about looking like a hermit; he releases her hand and replies that it has advantages. She vows to trim the beard one day and he answers we'll see.
They sit together over the herb book; Alexander points out a plant that eases swelling and Juliana says her mother wrote the same. She asks whether his scars came from war.
Alexander answers that some scars were from war and that it was terrible; his gaze turns heavy with past battles.
Juliana says she once thought losing wealth meant losing everything, then says perhaps she was wrong, while the two sit by the hearth.
Juliana holds a warm, peaceful gaze across the table as firelight flickers and the scene fades out.
